questions.title: Sphere falling through a liquid — viscosity, upthrust & forces

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Rearranging FD = 6πηrv gives η = FD/(6πrv). From F = ma, force has base units kg m s⁻²; r → m and v → m s⁻¹.
units of η = (kg m s⁻²)/(m × m s⁻¹) = kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Three arrows on the sphere: weight (W) vertically downwards; upthrust (U) vertically upwards; drag/viscous force (FD) vertically upwards. At terminal velocity the resultant force is zero, so the two upward arrows together balance the weight.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer:
At terminal velocity the forces balance: weight = upthrust + drag = 1.0 + 0.096 = 1.096 N
m = W/g = 1.096/9.81 = 0.11 kg

questions.title: Object projected onto a slope — kinematics & energy

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Displacement from a point is the distance in a straight line from the point in a given direction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: horizontal distance = ut = 6.0 × 0.71 = 4.3 m

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
s = ut + ½at², with u = 0 vertically:
s = ½ × 9.81 × 0.71² = 2.5 m

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
tanθ = (vertical distance)/(horizontal distance) = 2.5/4.3
θ = 30°

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.answer:
By conservation of energy, initial KE + loss of GPE = final KE:
½mv² = ½mu² + mgh → v² = u² + 2gh = 6.0² + 2 × 9.81 × 2.5 = 36 + 49.1 = 85.1
v = 9.2 m s⁻¹

questions.title: Force–extension graph of a sample — Hooke’s law & Young modulus

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The extension of a sample is proportional to the applied force (provided the limit of proportionality is not exceeded).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Draw a cross (×) labelled P on the graph at the limit of proportionality — the last point on the straight-line section, at approximately (60 mm, 5.4 N).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a cross (×) labelled E on the graph at the elastic limit — just beyond P where the curve starts to bend away from the straight line (the sample stops obeying Hooke’s law but is still elastic), at approximately (80 mm, 5.9 N).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: k = F/x = gradient of the straight-line section = 5.4/0.060 = 90 N m⁻¹

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: Work done = area under the force–extension graph up to the breaking point X. The region is roughly a triangle of base ≈ 0.20 m and height ≈ 10 N: area ≈ ½ × 0.20 × 10 ≈ 1.0 J (0.8–1.2 J acceptable).

parts.label: (e)
parts.answer: The spring constant of the second sample is greater. Since E = kL/A and both samples are the same material (same E) with the same length L, k is proportional to the cross-sectional area — so a larger area requires a greater force to produce the same extension.

questions.title: Transverse wave & ripple-tank interference — phase, frequency & superposition

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: R and T are separated by three-quarters of a wavelength (¾ of a cycle), so phase difference = 270°.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Draw an arrow at T pointing vertically downwards — T is on the section of the wave descending towards the next trough as the wave travels from left to right.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
R and T are ¾λ apart (phase difference 270°), so λ = 0.62 × (4/3) = 0.827 cm = 8.27×10⁻³ m
f = v/λ = 0.27/8.27×10⁻³ = 33 Hz

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: At P the waves from S1 and S2 superpose: the resultant displacement is the sum of the two displacements. A crest from one dipper meets a trough from the other (the waves arrive in antiphase, with a path difference of an odd number of half-wavelengths), so the waves destructively interfere and the amplitude of the resultant wave at P is zero (at all times).

questions.title: Cell with internal resistance — Kirchhoff’s laws & parallel resistors

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: The sum of the e.m.f.s around a closed loop is equal to the sum of the p.d.s around that loop (or: the algebraic sum of the e.m.f.s and p.d.s around a closed loop is zero).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: The conservation of energy (gives rise to Kirchhoff’s second law).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
By Kirchhoff’s first law, the current splits at the junction: I = I₁ + I₂. The resistors are in parallel, so each has the same p.d. V:
I = V/R₁ + V/R₂ and I = V/RT, hence V/RT = V/R₁ + V/R₂, so 1/RT = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Adding a resistor in parallel decreases the total resistance of the external circuit. Since I = E/(RT + r) and E and r are unchanged, the current in the cell increases.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: The larger current causes a larger p.d. drop across the internal resistance (Ir), so the terminal p.d. — the p.d. across the parallel resistors measured by the voltmeter — decreases.

questions.title: Samarium isotope — α decay, nuclide notation & quarks

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Nucleon number A = 62 + 85 = 147; proton number Z = 62.
¹⁴⁷₆₂Sm

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The spectrum shows a single sharp line: the emitted particles have discrete (one) kinetic-energy value(s), which is characteristic of α-particles. β-particles have a continuous range of kinetic energies, so the particles cannot be β.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
¹⁴⁷₆₂Sm → ¹⁴³₆₀Nd + ⁴₂α
(nucleon number: 147 = 143 + 4 ✓; proton number: 62 = 60 + 2 ✓)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
Up quark charge = +⅔e, bottom quark charge = −⅓e. Total charge is zero:
0 = +⅔e + (−⅓e) + q
q = −⅓e

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: A quark of charge −⅓e: the down (d) quark or the strange (s) quark.
